title: Angles: Straight Lines, Points, Triangles and Quadrilaterals

body_html:
How it works

Key facts:

  • Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
  • Angles around a point add up to 360°.
  • Vertically opposite angles (where two straight lines cross) are equal.
  • Angles in a triangle add up to 180°; in a quadrilateral, 360°.
  • An isosceles triangle has two equal sides and two equal base angles.
Example

Two angles on a straight line are 130° and x. Find x.

180 − 130 = 50.

Answer: x = 50°

Example

An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 40°. Find each base angle.

180 − 40 = 140.

140 ÷ 2 = 70.

Answer: 70°

Common mistakes

  • Using 360° for angles on a straight line, or 180° for angles around a point.
  • Thinking vertically opposite angles add up to 180°. They are equal.
  • Using 180° for a quadrilateral. It is 360°.
  • In an isosceles triangle, using the wrong pair of equal angles: the equal angles are at the ends of the base, opposite the equal sides.

faq.q: What do angles on a straight line add up to?
faq.a: 180°. If one angle is 130°, the other is 50°.
When two straight lines cross they make two pairs of opposite angles. The angles in each pair are equal.

faq.q: Why do the angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°?
faq.a: A diagonal splits any quadrilateral into two triangles, and each triangle has 180°.

faq.q: How do I find the angles in an isosceles triangle?
faq.a: The two base angles are equal. Take the top angle from 180° and halve the result.

items.q: What type of angle is 35°?
items.e: Acute: less than 90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°. So 35° is acute.

items.q: What type of angle is 90°?
items.e: Acute: less than 90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°. So 90° is right angle.

items.q: What type of angle is 128°?
items.e: Acute: less than 90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°. So 128° is obtuse.

items.q: What type of angle is 215°?
items.e: Acute: less than 90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°. So 215° is reflex.

items.q: What type of angle is 179°?
items.e: Acute: less than 90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°. So 179° is obtuse.

items.q: What type of angle is 300°?
items.e: Acute: less than 90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°. So 300° is reflex.

items.q: Angles on a straight line are 2x and 3x. Find x.
Angles around a point are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. Find x.
The angles of a triangle are x, x + 20 and x + 40. Find x.
Two angles in a triangle are 47° and 68°. What is the third angle?
A triangle has angles of 90° and 45°. What is the third angle?
items.e: 180 − 90 − 45 = 45°, so it is a right-angled isosceles triangle.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 90° and 115°. Find the fourth angle.
One angle where two straight lines cross is 64°. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The vertically opposite angle is also 64°. The other two are 180 − 64 = 116° each: 64°, 116° and 116°.

items.q: Each angle in an equilateral triangle is…
items.e: All three angles are equal: 180 ÷ 3 = 60°.

items.q: The two base angles of an isosceles triangle are each 52°. What is the third angle?
A kite has angles of 120°, 70° and 70°. What is the fourth angle?
Can a triangle have angles of 100° and 90°?
c: No, because 100 is not a multiple of 90
No, because 100° + 90° is already more than 180°
items.e: The three angles must add up to exactly 180°, and 100° + 90° = 190°. So no.

items.q: Ethan says the angles in a quadrilateral add up to 180°. Is he right?
items.e: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles: 2 × 180° = 360°.

items.q: What is the size of a full turn?
items.e: A full turn is 360°.

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand of a clock turn in 15 minutes?
items.e: 15 minutes is a quarter of a turn: 360 ÷ 4 = 90°.
